candidates.source_name: Asseco Central Europe – Referencie (client reference list, SK)
candidates.why_relevant: Asseco CE is the dominant Slovak core-banking/card-processing supplier (eStarBANK, Security Server, omnichannel). Its reference list names bank customers that never publish supplier identities themselves, so it maps otherwise-hidden private-bank sourcing relationships and is a snowball source for further actor names.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic crawl with browser-like headers / headless browser (plain fetch returned 403); diff reference entries per quarter, extract client names and solution names.
queries_used: Asseco Central Europe referencie banky Slovensko projekt tlačová správa
candidates.observed_blocker: WebFetch of https://ce.asseco.com/referencie/ returned HTTP 403 Forbidden (site indexed in search results, so presumed live but bot-defended; unverified)

candidates.source_name: Asseco Central Europe – Správy / press room (news releases, SK)
candidates.why_relevant: The winning supplier's own announcement is often the only public description of contract scope, technology and duration for Slovak bank deals; Asseco publishes SK-language releases on wins and go-lives.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Headless-browser crawl of paginated press index (/press/spravy/p/N/), store title+date+body; classify releases mentioning bank names.

brief: For Slovak banking and payments, the supplier side is the more talkative party: Asseco CE, PosAm, DATALAN, Alanata, SOFTEC, Printec, Euronet, Global Payments and Loomis all publish reference lists, case studies or service pages that reveal buyer relationships Slovak banks themselves keep quiet — a pattern explicitly documented in Slovak business press. Disclosure is split by tier: international vendors (Euronet, Worldline, Nexi, Diebold Nixdorf) announce deals in English on group IR/press pages with scope and duration, while Slovak integrators publish SK-language 'referencie' and 'prípadové štúdie' that often anonymise the bank as merely 'banka'. Practical collection therefore needs a browser-grade crawler (Asseco returned 403), group-level EN press polling plus SK media wires (SITA, TOUCHIT BrandIT) since local entities have no press feeds, and Wayback snapshots to catch references pruned when contracts lapse. The main residual weakness is verification: vendor claims are promotional and frequently buyer-anonymised, so this cell's output should be joined to award/tender records via each vendor's Slovak legal entity resolved through FinStat/ORSR.
